raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not like to spread myself too thin. On just 5.5 mu, I still keep both crops, but I will put more land into stevia because in recent years it has brought steadier cash than cotton if the field is managed cleanly. I have only two people at home, and my back is not as strong as before, so I will do what is familiar and not take big risks. Cotton can still make money, but it needs more watching for insects and more hand work when picking. Stevia also needs care, but if the seedlings establish well and I keep enough moisture from the well, it is worth it. So this year I will keep about 2 mu in cotton and 3.5 mu in stevia.

For cotton, I will plant in late April, about the same time as people around me. I will use seed that is easy to buy locally, not chase expensive special seed. I will put base fertilizer before planting, not too little, because if cotton starts weak it is hard to recover. If money gets tight, I would rather cut a little on pesticide than cut too much fertilizer. For stevia, I will plant after the weather turns warm and use purchased seedlings, because saved planting material is not as reliable. Stevia needs a clean field and steady water, so I will spend more on seedlings and a little more on topdressing after it gets going. I will irrigate both crops from the well, but not waste water because pumping costs money. I will mostly rely on family labor and only hire a little help if the weeds or harvest come all at once.
